Windowed self-attention (WSA) has become a strong back-
bone for single-image super-resolution (SR), yet its high
overhead often leads to latency inefficiency.

claims.text: The paper motivates its work by stating that windowed self-attention creates latency inefficiency in single-image super-resolution.

source_locator.quote:
The model retains the structural
intuition of Swin-based backbones but replaces all attention
modules with lightweight convolutional layers, combining
transformer-style token hierarchies with the efficiency and
stability of groupwise spatial convolutions.

claims.text: Swin-HIER retains a Swin-like hierarchy but replaces attention modules with lightweight convolutional layers that combine hierarchical tokens with groupwise spatial mixing.

claims.text: The paper cautions that higher PSNR does not necessarily correspond to higher perceptual quality, particularly in the high-PSNR regime.

method: Swin-HIER replaces attention with grouped depthwise-pointwise convolutional mixing inside a token-aligned hierarchical encoder-decoder, using symmetric padding, patch merging and expansion, aligned skip fusion, and PixelShuffle reconstruction.
problem: Swin-style single-image super-resolution has costly windowed self-attention and imperfect cross-window communication, creating latency and texture-consistency concerns for constrained deployment.
